clue.text: Religious leader embracing right, right? Right

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the head of the Roman Catholic Church
R is the standard abbreviation for right
a second abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks, then answers, whether a churchman holding conservative views is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'right's look like a stammer; the first two each give R, one held inside POPE and one tacked on the end, and the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, which is one everyday sense of right as an adjective.

clue.text: Dominant female has been changed following strange cut

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims off its final letter
something changed has been altered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: queer means strange; cut short it loses its last letter
the word been, rearranged

explanation.surface: A domineering woman has changed her ways after an odd snub.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'following' puts the reworked part after the cut-down word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee is the fertile female ruling a hive, and figuratively a woman who dominates her social circle.

clue.text: Counselled about conclusions of the lower court being made known

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter, taken from each word that follows
about here means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: counselled means advised
the final letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: Legal advice given about the verdicts of an inferior court being publicised.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters sit inside the word for counselled, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise something is to publicise it, so something advertised has been made known to the public.

clue.text: Kind of painting or photograph put on biography

blocks.note: a still is a single photograph, especially one from a film
a written life is a biography

explanation.surface: Asking what genre of picture or photo goes alongside a life story.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above, so the photograph word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a genre of painting showing inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers arranged on a table.

clue.text: Part of speech, in short, to get ready for theatre

blocks.note: first meaning: a shortened form of the grammatical term preposition
second meaning: prepare a patient for surgery

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in brief, then an actor getting ready for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre here is the hospital operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Prep abbreviates preposition, and as a verb it means preparing a patient before an operation.

clue.text: Means to raise a large wild animal

blocks.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: How you might rear an enormous beast from the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means to raise' sounds like rearing an animal but is a lifting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild dog-like carnivore of Africa and Asia, a typical example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Reduction, as incorporated in formal ruling

indicators.note: to be incorporated in something is to be taken inside its body

blocks.note: a decree is an official order
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut written into an official judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a lessening in amount, the same as a reduction.

clue.text: Simplify calculation by increasing number in assembly

blocks.note: first meaning: raise a figure to the next whole number
second meaning: a gathering together of people or cattle

explanation.surface: Making sums easier by bumping figures upward at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up a figure is to raise it to a neater value; a round-up is also a collecting together of animals or people.

clue.text: Singular source of pressure, possibly, for noble person

blocks.note: first meaning: one equal, the single source of the group pressure named after such equals
second meaning: a member of the nobility, such as a lord

explanation.surface: A lone cause of stress perhaps acting on an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half points at the phrase for pressure from your equals, taking just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the British nobility, while peers in the plural are your equals in age or status.

clue.text: Theory oddly selected by people in street

indicators.note: picking oddly means keeping the letters in the first, third and fifth places

blocks.note: letters one, three and five of the word
a race is a people sharing descent

explanation.surface: A notion picked out at random by residents of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrace is a row of joined houses, and in Britain many street names end in Terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses forming a street, which is why so many British street names use the word.

clue.text: I.e. place being rebuilt around me bit by bit

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so its letters are rearranged
around means surrounding, so the reworked letters go outside the remaining word

blocks.note: the letters of i.e. and place, rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Explaining that a building is being reconstructed around the speaker a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal describes something done in stages or parts rather than all at once.

clue.text: Game that's handled by person in hot seat?

definitions.text: that's handled by person in hot seat?

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game played for stakes

blocks.clueFragment: that's handled by person in hot seat?
blocks.note: second meaning: a metal rod gripped by someone sitting at the fireside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot seat' suggests a pressured player but here is a chair by the hearth, where the fire iron is held.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game, and also the iron rod used to stir up a fire in a grate.

clue.text: Disprove final 20% of conjecture, however

indicators.note: one fifth of a ten-letter word means keeping its closing two letters

blocks.note: the word has ten letters, so the last fifth is its final pair
but and however are synonyms

explanation.surface: Knocking down the tail end of a theory, even so.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it with evidence, the same as to disprove it.

clue.text: Plant old bishop and priest put in US city

indicators.note: putting something in a place means it ends up inside it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B is the chess notation for bishop
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A seedling, an elderly cleric and a clergyman sent off to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often grown for its blue blooms in hanging baskets.

clue.text: Pub repeatedly is disrupted by an uncivilised lot

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into, so the word is split by another going inside

blocks.note: bar means pub, given twice
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tavern keeps having its peace broken by a rowdy crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarians are uncivilised or brutish people, the plural matching the collective lot.

clue.text: Falsified logs of former product of mine that's deceptive

indicators.note: something falsified has been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of logs and of, rearranged
old means former, as in an old boss

explanation.surface: Doctored records about a past mining output that misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Fool's gold is iron pyrite, a mineral dug from mines that looks like gold and fools prospectors.

clue.text: Smooth, cold, and undecided about HM in session with reporters

indicators.note: about here means around, so the phrase is wrapped round what follows

blocks.note: to press clothes is to smooth them
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
sitting on the fence means being undecided
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A flattering, chilly and noncommittal account of the monarch given at a media briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal letters sit inside the fence phrase, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is a meeting at which a figure answers questions from journalists.

clue.text: Not advocating war, if one's in treaty

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a pact is a treaty
taken as written
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: Arguing against conflict, provided you have signed an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist opposes war and violence, so the word works as an adjective meaning anti-war.

clue.text: With audacity, learner joins expert making piece of jewellery

blocks.note: neck is informal British for cheek or nerve
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A cheeky apprentice teams up with a master craftsman to create a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is an ornament worn around the neck, a common item of jewellery.

clue.text: Key detail wrong for place of refuge

indicators.note: if something is wrong it is out of order, so these letters need rearranging

blocks.note: C is a musical key
the letters of detail, rearranged

explanation.surface: An important particular is mistaken about a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, a stronghold where people take refuge.

clue.text: Assuming game for children includes family

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within

blocks.note: tag is a chasing game played by children
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Presuming a playground game involves relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking on, say, a role or responsibility is assuming it, so the two present participles match.

clue.text: English course including a non-English person

blocks.note: taken as written
a Scot is a Briton who is not English

explanation.surface: An English lesson that admits a foreign student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a class but means a racecourse; Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in England, home of the Royal Ascot race meeting.

clue.text: Expert navigator needed in fleet as mandated

indicators.note: needed in signals the letters are found within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A skilled seafarer is required by naval order.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch explorer who sailed to Tasmania and New Zealand, an expert navigator.

clue.text: Fighting power that's corrupt

blocks.note: war is armed fighting
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Military might that has gone rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp something is to twist or pervert it, which is a verb sense of corrupt.

clue.text: King taken in by light-headed religious ascetic

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being drawn inside it

blocks.note: fair-haired, so having a light-coloured head
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A monarch fooled by a dizzy holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-headed' suggests dizziness, but it means having blond hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu holy man who lives by begging and self-denial, an ascetic.

clue.text: Attack with ultimate in air support

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last one

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
aid means support

explanation.surface: An assault backed by the best possible air cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack on an enemy position or premises.

clue.text: Flower that makes one happy when it's cut

definitions.text: Flower that makes one happy when it's cut

blocks.clueFragment: Flower that makes one happy when it's cut
blocks.note: surface reading: a bloom that cheers whoever receives it once picked for a vase
setter's reading: shorten this flower's name and what is left is a word meaning happy

explanation.walkthrough: Cut flowers are those picked for display, but the cut here is to the word: chop off the end of the name and the first four letters mean pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a tall garden flower with sword-shaped leaves, often known as a glad.

clue.text: Times can be read on this – other paper put back

definitions.text: Times can be read on this

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the word reads in reverse

blocks.note: a newspaper other than the Times named earlier in the clue
laid paper is a writing paper with a ribbed texture

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader is told to return some other journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' poses as the newspaper but in the definition means hours of the day; 'other' then points to a rival paper, The Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial shows the hour by the shadow cast on its face, so times of day are read from it.

clue.text: Criticise article about expert that deals with all complaints

blocks.note: to pan is to review harshly
an ace is an expert
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Slamming an item about a specialist who handles every grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The article ends up after the expert, so 'about' only loosely places it; read it as the article coming round the expert's far side.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for all ills, and complaints here means illnesses rather than grievances.
